plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden flower heads that follow the sun across the sky. Fields of them turn whole hillsides into seas of yellow, and bees crowd the dark, seed-filled centers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Central and southern Europe and the Great Plains of North America
plants.funFact: What looks like one flower is really hundreds of tiny florets packed into a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Moorlands and heaths blush purple as countless tiny bell-shaped blooms open along wiry stems. The result is a soft, honey-scented carpet that glows in late-summer light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Scottish Highlands, northern England and moorlands across northern Europe
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture, and the plant was once used to stuff mattresses and thatch roofs.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere's late winter, this Australian tree bursts into fluffy golden pom-pom blooms. They scent the air with a sweet fragrance and brighten the bushland while much of the country is still cool.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring there.
